title: Mom's Shopping List
text:
Mom wrote this shopping list and stuck it on the fridge. I added a few things when she was not looking.

Mom's list: milk, eggs, bread, twelve bananas, cheese, dish soap, a big bag of {plural noun}, and exactly {number} jars of jam.

My list: a {adjective} balloon, something {color} for the cat, a box of {plural noun}, and a giant {noun} for my baby brother.

At the store, Mom found my part of the list. She laughed {adverb} and said I could pick one thing. I picked the balloon. Then she let me push the cart, and I {past tense verb} all the way down the cereal aisle.

The cashier, Mr. Ray, said my balloon was very {adjective}. He gave me a sticker shaped like a {noun}.

Next week, I get to write the whole list by myself. I am going to write it {adverb} and put {plural noun} at the very top.

title: Attention, Shoppers!
text:

title: The Day I Pushed the Cart
text:
Dear Diary,

Today Dad let me push the grocery cart all by myself.

The cart had one wheel that squeaked {adverb} no matter what I did. In the fruit section, I picked out {number} apples and a {adjective} pineapple.

Next we went to the dairy aisle. Dad needed milk, yogurt, {plural noun}, and a block of cheese the size of a {noun}. I put everything in the cart next to the {plural noun}.

In the cereal aisle, I saw a box with a {animal} on the front. Dad said we could get it if I promised to {verb} after dinner.

Then I parked the cart {adverb} by the bread. A lady said my driving was very {adjective}.

At the checkout, I put the eggs on the belt while {verb ending in ing}. The cashier said I was the best cart driver of the day. I {past tense verb} all the way to the car.

Next time, Dad says I can help pick out the {plural noun}.

Love,
Owen

title: A Letter to the Store Manager
text:
Dear Store Manager,

My name is Lily. I shop at your store every Sunday with my grandpa and my {adjective} little brother. My favorite part is the aisle with all the {plural noun}. Here are my ideas.

Idea one: Every cart should have a little horn that goes "{sound}" so people know you are coming.

Idea two: Please play more music. Shoppers would love to {verb} in the frozen food aisle. It would keep them warm.

Idea three: You should sell {adjective} bananas.

Idea four: The person who gives out free {food} samples should also give out {plural noun}. Grandpa {past tense verb} when I told him this one.

Idea five: Please put a {noun} in every aisle for kids who get tired.

Thank you to Miss Rosa at the checkout. She always talks {adverb} to me. Last week she gave me a sticker of a {noun}, and I put it on my {body part}.

Please think about my ideas while you are {verb ending in ing}.

Your friend,
Lily

text:

text:

You must be able to: Lift a box as heavy as a {noun}, smile at every customer, and {verb} when the radio plays a good song.

title: Rules for Being a Store Helper
text:
Mom says I am her official grocery helper, so here are the rules.

Rule one: Stay close to the cart. If you stop to look at the {plural noun} for too long, Mom will make you hold the list.

Rule two: Only put things in the cart that are on the list. Last week I put a {adjective} {noun} in the cart, and Mom found it at the checkout.

Rule three: Use your inside voice. If you need to sneeze, sneeze {adverb} into your {body part}.

Rule four: Help carry the bags. I can carry {number} bags of {plural noun} at once.

Rule six: Say thank you to the cashier. Mr. Ray always says "{silly word}!" back to me.

Rule seven: If you are a very good helper, you get to {verb} on the way home. Today I was the best helper, so I {past tense verb} the whole way while {verb ending in ing}.

title: My Interview with Ms. Bell
text:

Q: What do you do on your break?

Q: What is the hardest part of your job?
